text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- A powerful bomb apparently aimed at the head of Bulgaria's business conglomerate Multigroup wrecked his car on a mountain road outside Sofia at around 1 a.m. on Tuesday but no one was hurt, the Interior Minnistry said in a statement. @

-- The shareholders of Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim did not approve the company's 1996 annual report, following a cabinet's decision from Monday to launch an audit of the plant's accounts.

-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov and Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah negotiated a $129 million credit from Kuwait's Arab Economic Cooperation Fund for the Balkan country to support its reforms.
Stoyanov was on a three-day official visit to Kuwait and is due back to Bulgaria on Wednesday. @

-- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright rejected a suggestion by her Bulgarian counterpart Nadezhda Mihailova that NATO designate Bulgaria as a likely candidate for future membership in the alliance.
-- Bulgaria's Zemedelie state agricultural fund is to extend subsidies of 1.5 billion levs for this year's wheat harvesting, the fund's executive director Nikola Nikolov said.

-- The head of Bulgaria's get-rich-quick scheme East West International Holding Group Ivo Nedialkov, a target of an international arrest warrant for obtaining some $10 million by fraud was extradided from France to Bulgaria.
-- Bulgaria's 168 Chasa press group, majority owned by Germany's conglomerate Westdeutsche Algemeine Zeitung Group, owed 15 billion levs of unpaid customs duties, Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's ruling Union of Democratic Forces proposed that parliament holds extraordinary sessions by end-June to approve the 1997 budget prior to introduction of a tough fixed exchange rate regime, known as currency board, from July 1. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
